I have been farming this land for 50 years. I am 70 now, never went to school, and everything I know came from my father’s hands and from watching what works on the fields around me. My farm is 13.1 mu — not small, not huge — and it is just me and my old woman working it. We have a well, so I can pump water when I need it, but diesel for the pump costs money, so I count every time I turn it on.

This year I will do what I did last year, because last year gave me a decent harvest and change is dangerous. For wheat, I sow in October. I use improved seed, about 30 jin per mu, the same kind my neighbor Lao Zhang bought from the shop and did well with. Before sowing, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 50 kg per mu. When the wheat greens up in spring, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once in winter if the ground is dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and insecticide twice when I see bugs flying around. I rotary till before planting. If the weather is normal, I expect about 1000 to 1100 jin per mu, around 550 kg.

For maize, after we cut the wheat in June, I plant right away. There is no time to plow deep — I plant no-tillage, straight into the stubble. I use hybrid seed, one package per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu. When the plants are knee-high, I add urea, about 20 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come. I spray pesticide three times in total — herbicide once, insecticide twice. I expect about 1200 jin per mu, around 600 kg.

Fertilizer is expensive, every bag is real money out of my pocket. But a bad harvest is worse than wasting some fertilizer. If I am not sure whether I put enough, I add a little more rather than risk losing yield. Lao Zhang uses about the same amounts as me, so I copy him. If everyone around you does something, you do it too.
